mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate is held constant above 5.25% for two consecutive months, the S&P 500 forward 60-day return is expected to be negative due to persistent discount rate stickiness and reduced risk appetite.
failure_condition: Over a 60-day window following the trigger, SPX 60-day forward returns are not statistically different from the prior 60-day average (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a labor market strengthening that boosts equity valuations and drives positive 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >10% in a month AND UNRATE falls by >0.2 percentage points in the same month
failure_condition: In 80% of similar labor market strengthening events, the 20-day forward return is non-positive (quantile regression).

mechanism_narrative: When consumer demand indicators (HOUST) and industrial production (INDPRO) both exceed their 12-month moving averages for two consecutive months, the S&P 500 is expected to post a positive 5-day forward return as market anticipates sustained economic expansion.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 12-month MA and INDPRO > 12-month MA for two consecutive months
regime_hint: Dual momentum in demand and supply indicators
failure_condition: Across 50 such dual-momentum events, the 5-day forward return is negative on average (mean < 0).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) followed by a subsequent rebound exceeding the prior month's level predicts a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return as market anticipates persistent supply-side weakness.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by >5% in a month AND INDPRO rises in the following month by >5% above prior month
failure_condition: In 70% of prior similar supply cycle patterns, the 20-day forward return is non-negative (quantile regression).

mechanism_narrative: Persistent inflation acceleration (CPIAUCSL rising by >0.5% month-on-month for three consecutive months) is associated with a negative 60-day S&P 500 forward return as investors anticipate rate hikes and equity discount rates rise.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL month-on-month increase > 0.5% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: Over 40 such inflation accelerations, the 60-day forward return is not statistically lower than during stable inflation periods (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in unemployment (UNRATE) below 3.5% followed by a sustained rise in labor market participation (PAYEMS) predicts a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as market anticipates a robust labor market.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 3.5% AND PAYEMS increases by >2% in the following month
regime_hint: Labor market transition to full employment
failure_condition: Across 30 analogous episodes, the 20-day forward return is negative in >70% of cases (bootstrap confidence interval excludes zero).

mechanism_narrative: When retail sales (HOUST) fall by more than 3% in a month with no recovery in industrial production (INDPRO), the S&P 500 is expected to show a negative 5-day forward return as risk aversion rises on demand weakness.
candidate_trigger: HOUST falls by >3% in a month AND INDPRO does not exceed prior month's value
failure_condition: In 50 such demand weakness events, the 5-day forward return is not statistically lower than during neutral periods (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in Treasury yields (implied by FEDFUNDS < 1.5%) during a non-inflationary macro regime predicts a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return as lower discount rates boost equity present value.
failure_condition: During 40 such low-inflation FEDFUNDS periods, the 60-day forward return is not statistically higher than during high-inflation periods (t-test p > 0.05).
